Python functions for building app and dashboard UIs. Each function returns a plain dict that the frontend renders as a real UI block — 81 builders organized by category (usable on @aiui.page, in zero-code YAML, and inline inside chat via await aiui.send_block(...)). Looking for visual examples in both Python and zero-code YAML? Browse the UI Components gallery.

A data table. In the app shell it sorts by header click, formats typed columns, and can search, page, link rows and open a row in a side panel. The old call shape keeps working unchanged. A larger table with typed columns, dict rows and search: Parameter Type Required Description headers Sequence[str] ✅ unless columns Column header labels rows Sequence[Sequence \ dict] ✅ Row arrays in column order, or dicts keyed by column key (sent as arrays) columns Sequence[str \ dict] — Column config (below). Gives the headers when headers is not set row_ids Sequence[str] — Stable unique ID per row. Makes rows selectable by click, Enter or Space actions Sequence[str] — Row action button labels (requires row_ids) searchable bool — A search box that keeps the rows holding every typed word (in the browser) page_size int — Rows per page; 0 shows every row. Unset: 50 per page once there are more than 100 rows sortable bool — False turns header sorting off. Default on row_href_key str — Key (in dict rows, or a column key) holding each row's link. The first cell becomes the link and a click on the row opens it row_detail bool — A click (or Enter) on a row opens a side panel listing the row's fields detail_key str — Key in dict rows holding a list of block dicts the side panel renders instead of the fields (implies row_detail) detail_load_key str — Key in dict rows holding a lazy section key loaded via POST /api/pages/{id}/action ({"_lazy": key, "_params": ...}) when that row's side panel opens (implies row_detail) detail_load str — Prefix for lazy row detail keys (f"{detail_load}{row_id_or_index}"; implies row_detail) max_height int \ str — Height of the scrolling body (px or CSS length, 0 for none). Default 70vh, so the header stays in view caption str — Accessible name of the table and its search box Column dict keys: key, label, type, format, decimals, tones, tone_above, tone_below, thresholds, href_key, width (px or CSS length), align (left, center, right) and sortable (False for one column). A plain string is a column whose key and label are that string. type Cell value Shows auto (default) anything Text as sent; a column of numbers lines up at the end; {"text", "href"} is a link and {"src", "alt"} an image text any The value as text number number (or {"value", "tone"}) Right-aligned, tabular figures. format: compact (1.2k, 3.4M), percent (a fraction: 0.123 → 12.3%), multiplier or x (2.3x), fixed (exactly decimals, default 2); none groups digits. decimals sets the fraction digits. Optional threshold colouring: tone_above (number or [n, tone], default success), tone_below (number or [n, tone], default error), or ordered thresholds: [{"gte": 1, "tone": "success"}, {"lt": 0.5, "tone": "error"}] link {"text", "href", "external"} or a URL; or text with the column's href_key A link. Only http(s), mailto, tel and relative URLs are kept badge text, or {"text", "tone"} A badge; tones maps a value to success, warning, error or info tag a list (or comma-separated text) One badge per item, toned like badge image URL, or {"src", "alt"} A small rounded thumbnail (format: "wide" for 16:9); alt defaults to the column label progress 0..1 A bar and its percent date ISO text, or epoch seconds or ms Nov 22, 2026 in UTC; format: "datetime" adds the time, "iso" gives 2026-11-22. Sorts by time sparkline a list of numbers A small trend line (no axes); sorts by the last point A header click sorts ascending, descending, then back to the server's order: stable, numeric-aware (1,234, 1.2k, 12%, 2.5x), empty cells last; headers are buttons with aria-sort. On a phone the table scrolls sideways. The legacy dashboard style draws the dict as a plain text table. With row_ids, the dashboard renderer emits bubbling DOM events from the table, so a custom view can own query state (search, filters, page, sort) and react to rows: Event detail aiui:table-select {rowId, index} aiui:table-action {action, rowId} Because events carry the stable rowId, selection stays correct after the server re-sorts or filters rows. Loading, empty and error states compose from existing components (aiui.skeleton(), aiui.empty(), aiui.alert()):

A chart with tooltips, colours from the theme's --chart-1..5 tokens (light and dark) and the full width of its column, down to a phone. The chart library loads in its own chunk the first time a page shows a chart. Parameter Type Default Description title str "" Chart title data list[dict] [] Rows, e.g. [{"month": "Jan", "views": 1200}]. A histogram also takes plain numbers chart_type str "bar" bar (columns), barh (horizontal bars), line, area, scatter, pie, donut, histogram, heatmap, sparkline kind str — Alias of chart_type x str first text column Category key. Scatter: the x value (default: first numeric column). Histogram: the measured value y str \ list[str] every numeric column Series key, or keys for several series y2 str — A secondary series drawn as faint bars on its own scale (bar, barh, line, area) labels dict[str, str] — Display names for keys in the legend and tooltip label str — Scatter: key naming each point in the tooltip tooltip list[str \ dict] — Extra row keys (or {"key", "label", "format"} dicts) shown in the tooltip (including scatter & heatmap) stacked bool False Stack the series (bar, barh, area) reference number, list of numbers, {value, label} or a list of them — Dashed reference lines (a vertical line on barh) color_by_reference bool False Bars at or above the first reference keep the series colour; bars below it are muted x_format, y_format str — number (1,234.5), compact (1.2k, 3.4M), percent (0.25 → 25%), multiplier (1.5x), duration (seconds → 1:05). Axis ticks default to compact, tooltips to number x_domain, y_domain [min, max] auto X / value axis range, e.g. x_domain=[1e3, 1e7] on scatter or y_domain=[0, 1] with y_format="percent" x_scale, y_scale str "linear" "linear" or "log" (non-positive values are omitted safely) clip bool \ number \ [min, max] — Clamp outliers to x_domain/y_domain (True), an upper cap (number), or [min, max] (histogram edge bins show ≤/+; heatmap colour scale clamps to bounds) bins int Sturges' rule (max 30) Histogram bin count height int 240 Plot height in px; barh grows with its rows, pie and donut are 260 caption str — A line of muted text under the chart legend bool more than one series Show the legend value str "value" Heatmap: the cell value key. x is the column key and y the row key (defaults x and y) facet str — Key whose values split the rows into small charts in a responsive grid (at most 24 panels) facet_scales str "shared" "shared" (one value scale across all panels) or "free" (each panel scales to its own data) Heatmap. Columns and rows keep the order they first appear in data, so sort the rows (Mon..Sun, 0..23) before passing them; a repeated cell sums. Cells are coloured on a sequential scale from the theme's first chart colour (light and dark), empty cells are outlined, y_format formats the values in the tooltip and the colour scale under the grid, and y_domain fixes the scale. Cells keep a minimum width, so a wide grid scrolls sideways inside the chart on a phone. Sparkline. One series, no axes, the last value printed beside it; height defaults to 48 px. A number list under a metric is aiui.metric(..., sparkline=[...]). Small multiples. With facet, each panel is 160 px high (48 for a sparkline) unless height is set, panels follow first-seen order, and the legend is shown once. y_domain overrides the shared scale. An unknown chart_type or format raises ValueError. A dict written by hand ({"type": "chart", "data": [...], "chart_type": "line"}) works too: missing keys are inferred from the first row, and column, hbar and doughnut are accepted as kind names. At most 5,000 rows are drawn. The legacy dashboard style shows a summary card instead of the chart.

A metric card with optional delta indicator and caption. benchmark compares a numeric value with a reference: a ratio of 2 or more reads as a multiple ("17x below median"), a smaller one as a percentage ("25% above median"), and it is coloured like a delta (delta_color applies, so "inverse" makes "above" the loss). sparkline draws the numbers as a tiny trend line under the value. A delta that starts with +/↑ or -/↓ (or a signed number) is coloured as a gain or a loss. Use caption for a neutral note under the value, so a subtitle such as "-2 from plan" is not coloured by accident. Parameter Type Required Default Description label str ✅ — Metric label value Any ✅ — Main metric value delta str ❌ None Change indicator (e.g. "+5%") delta_color str ❌ "normal" "normal" (rise is good), "inverse" (fall is good, e.g. "-3 days"), or "off" (never coloured) caption str ❌ None Neutral note under the value, never coloured. help is an alias sparkline list[float] ❌ None Numbers drawn as a tiny trend line under the value benchmark float ❌ None Reference the value is compared with ("17x below median") benchmark_label str ❌ "benchmark" Name of the benchmark in that line

App HTML or SVG (a chart, a styled box, a small interactive widget), isolated from the page. Parameter Type Required Default Description content str ✅ — HTML string; may hold , and height int\ str ❌ None Fixed height (pixels or a CSS length such as "20rem"). Default: fit the content csp str ❌ None Content-Security-Policy for the frame, replacing the default below trusted bool ❌ False Render inline in the page instead of in a frame, sanitised (see below) title str ❌ None Accessible name of the frame (default "Embedded content") Security model Default (sandboxed frame). In the app shell the content renders in an built from srcdoc, without allow-same-origin. Its scripts run in an opaque origin: they cannot read or change the app's page, cookies, localStorage or session, cannot call /api/* as the signed-in user, cannot open pop-ups, submit forms or navigate the top window. A also blocks network access. The default policy is default-src 'none'; img-src data: https:; style-src 'unsafe-inline'; script-src 'unsafe-inline'; font-src data:; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'none'. Pass csp= to tighten or loosen it; the frame sizes itself with a small inline script, so a policy without script-src 'unsafe-inline' needs a fixed height. trusted=True (inline). The content is placed in the page through the sanitised Markdown pipeline (rehype-sanitize): scripts, event handlers, style, and are removed. Use it for simple markup (tables, lists, links) that should flow with the page text; use the default frame for SVG and anything with scripts. Never put untrusted text into raw HTML yourself. Escape values you interpolate (html.escape(...)) even inside the frame: an injected script cannot reach the app, but it can still change what the frame shows. Legacy dashboard style. html renders in the same sandboxed frame (fixed height, default 320 px). html_embed there still sets the HTML directly on the page, where scripts and inline handlers run: pass only content you wrote. #### Theme variables These CSS custom properties are defined on the page in both themes and copied into every html frame, where they follow light/dark changes live: Variable Meaning --aiui-fg Body text --aiui-muted Secondary text, axis labels --aiui-border Hairlines, grid lines --aiui-bg Page background --aiui-surface Card / panel background --aiui-accent Brand accent (follows the theme preset) --aiui-success / --aiui-warning / --aiui-danger / --aiui-info Status colours --aiui-font / --aiui-font-mono Font stacks The frame's body already uses --aiui-fg and --aiui-font and has a transparent background, so plain HTML matches the page.

Components are designed to compose. Use columns() for horizontal layout within a layout():

On submit the form POSTs every input by name (else label) as JSON to /api/pages/{page}/action, handled by @aiui.register_page_action(action); action is normally the page id. If the handler returns a block tree (aiui.layout([...]), i.e. {"_components": [...]}) the page re-renders with it; a reply with message shows a toast instead. submit_on_change=True submits whenever an input changes: right away for selects, pills, chips, checkboxes and dates, 400 ms after the last keystroke for text. A submit with the same values as the last one is skipped, and a change made while one is in flight posts once more when it returns. Leave it off for a form whose button starts a job; mark single inputs with auto_submit=True instead.

Parameter Type Required Default Description action str ❌ "" Action id (normally the page id; optional with method="get") inputs Sequence[dict] ✅ — Input components chips bool ❌ True Show active filters as removable chips defaults dict ❌ None Reset value per input name ({"start", "end"} for a date range) reset_label str ❌ "Reset" Label of the control that clears all filters method str ❌ "post" "get" writes filter values into the page URL and re-fetches page data (no action handler needed) update_url bool ❌ False With method="post", also write submitted values into the page URL after a successful action A compact wrapping row (a search landmark) that posts like form with submit_on_change. Under it, each active filter is a chip ("Channel: Ann ×", one chip per value of a list); the × posts the form with that filter reset, and Reset posts all of them reset. A filter is active when its value differs from its reset value: defaults[name], else the first option of a select, radio or single segmented input, else empty; number and slider inputs only when defaults names them. Chips are read from the values the server sent, so the handler must return the page rebuilt from the posted values. A full example: examples/python/32-filter-page/app.py. tags_input, date_range_input, segmented_input and filter_bar render in the app shell (the default style); the legacy dashboard style shows them as JSON.

Understanding how components flow from Python to the browser.

Python: Call aiui.card("Revenue", value="$1,500") — returns a dict: Server: @aiui.page() handler returns aiui.layout([...]): API: GET /api/pages/{id}/data returns the JSON Frontend: dashboard.js detects _components key and calls renderComponents(): Renderer: renderComponent(comp) dispatches on comp.type: DOM: Each renderer creates HTML elements with db-* CSS classes
The magic key that triggers structured rendering: aiui.layout(children) automatically wraps children in {"_components": [...]}.
Every component function returns a dict with: Key Required Description type ✅ Component type name (e.g. "card", "table") Other keys Varies Component-specific properties

All components use db-* prefixed CSS classes: Component CSS Class Card .db-card, .db-card-title, .db-card-value, .db-card-footer Table .db-viewer table Alert .db-alert, .db-alert-info, .db-alert-success, etc. Badge .db-badge, .db-badge-secondary, .db-badge-destructive Tabs .db-tabs, .db-tab-list, .db-tab-btn, .db-tab-panel
